title: Memory Read/Write Portable Intent
description: Write one PSS read-after-write memory intent and inspect the generated UVM sequence and C bare-metal equivalents.

steps.title: Step 1: Constrain the Write's Buffer
steps.instructions: Open `starter/mem_test.pss`. In `write_mem`'s `legal_write` constraint, make the output buffer's address 4-byte aligned and keep its data in the range 0x0000 to 0xFFFF. Use PSS syntax: set membership is `in`, not `inside`. Check yourself: which field names do your constraints refer to, and why do they live on `wr` rather than in `read_verify`?

steps.title: Step 2: Bind Read-Verify to the Write
steps.instructions: Give `read_verify` a buffer input named `rd`. In `mem_read_write_test`'s activity, traverse the write and then the read with the labels `wr_a` and `rd_a`, and bind the read's input to the write's output so the read consumes exactly that buffer. Then fill the four `exec body` templates: SV templates wrapped in `begin ... end` that start `mem_write_seq` and `mem_read_seq` on `p_sequencer.mem_sqr` (the read reports `PSS_MEM_VERIFY` on a mismatch), and C templates that call `mem_write32()`, `mem_read32()` and `test_fail()`.

steps.title: Step 3: Compare Generated Targets
steps.instructions: Predict first: if you delete the `bind`, what may the tool do with the read's input? Write your answer down, then check it against the README's Expected Outcome. Compare the generated UVM and C excerpts in the README (the full files in `solution/` unlock when you finish): find where each `exec body` template and each solved value from your constraints appears in both targets, and note that the tool prints bit values in decimal.
